title: Regime Structure and Entropic Flow Ontology in Discrete Gravity Models
short_title: Regime Structure and Entropic Flow Ontology
epistemic_status: Foundational framework establishing regime-based ontology for discrete entropic gravity models
abstract: Formalises the regime structure underlying discrete entropic gravity models based on graph-defined functionals. Distinct physical behaviours (UV/Newtonian, IR/MOND-like, Cosmological/Yukawa) emerge from dominance transitions between gradient, bulk, and source sectors of a discrete entropic functional. Λ functions as a bulk capacity parameter governing large-scale screening. Provides regime-based foundation without assuming a fundamental spacetime metric.

structural_features: No free functions beyond μ(x) and μ_Λ ∝ Λ
Defined on graph topology; no continuum metric assumed

key_equations.discrete_functional: F[Φ] = Σ κ_ij F(|Φ_i−Φ_j|/a₀) + Σ ½μ_Λ(Φ_i−Φ_V)² + Σ λ_i ρ_i Φ_i
key_equations.screening_scale: L_Λ = 1/√μ_Λ, μ_Λ ∝ Λ → L_Λ ∝ Λ⁻¹/² ~ 4.4 Gpc

ontological_commitments.entropy: Functional capacity of the discrete network, not thermodynamic entropy
ontological_commitments.energy_flow: Gradient energy redistribution on the graph
ontological_commitments.lambda: Bulk entropic capacity — anchoring strength to cosmological background Φ_V
ontological_commitments.spacetime: Emergent from graph structure, not fundamental
ontological_commitments.time: Equilibrium condition δF/δΦ_i = 0; dynamics is relaxation

open_problems: Derivation of temporal dynamics from functional
falsification_criteria: Three regimes fail to be exhaustive for any field configuration
Transitions require additional free functions beyond μ(x) and μ_Λ ∝ Λ
Λ cannot simultaneously set a₀ and L_Λ consistently
Numerical verification in companion papers becomes inconsistent
